answer: Practically, the chain should score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because gale only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, echo is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any island approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
